facts.fact: The Universal Service and Access Fund, funded by mandatory contributions from telecom operators and administered by USAASA, was collecting money: the department's entities collected R249 million in 2021-22 rising to R281 million in 2025-26, R1.2 billion over the five years (The Citizen, citing a parliamentary reply).

The fund's expenditure is given as R1.08 billion against R1.6 billion in rollover funds, with R567 million of digital migration inventory written off in the last financial year (2025-26); the story gives collections and spending but does not name the year beside the R1.08 billion, so the latest year is taken from context.

ICASA collected R1,287,583,749 for the Universal Service and Access Fund over 2021/22 to 2025/26, R281,177,935 in 2025/26 and R251,411,657 in 2024/25, per the Minister's oral reply to question 763; USAASA administers the spending.

The fund's actual expenditure in 2025/26 was R1,087.904 million against R54.987 million DCDT drawdown and R1,685 million rollover funds, leaving about R652.083 million unspent; both collections and spending are given, the spending figure supplied by USAASA.

The fund's actual expenditure in 2024/25 was R769.092 million against R52.629 million DCDT drawdown and R1,270 million rollover funds, per the Minister's reply; collections for the year were R251.4 million.
